text:
Special period or not, we welcome your careful letter and we are sorry your recent trip left you uneasy. You said the pet handling process felt inconsistent, the guidance was not as clear as it should have been, and the transfer of your carrier seemed rougher than safe practice allows. That is a fair complaint, and it is the kind we take seriously at Aurelia Skyways.

From the safety side, the normal standard is simple: passengers receive clear guidance before departure, the safety coordinator checks the main hazards and the prevention steps, the ground team moves carriers carefully between services, and every animal gets patient attention from trained staff. When that chain slips, even once, the experience can feel alarming. We do not dismiss that.

I have reviewed the issue as a routine desk matter, and the point that stands out is communication. If a traveler leaves with mixed instructions, the whole process becomes harder to trust. That is on us to fix. We are reinforcing the briefing language used at handoff, so the same plain advice is given every time and nothing important is left to chance. We are also reminding staff that carrier handling must stay smooth, level, and unhurried, with extra care when an animal is stressed or alert.

Your note also helps us watch for small lapses that can grow into bigger safety concerns if nobody speaks up. The Companion Animal Travel Desk depends on that kind of feedback. It lets us correct habits before they become patterns. We want the experience to feel calm, predictable, and respectful from check-in through arrival.

If you fly with us again, please let the desk know any special handling needs early, and we will keep the focus on the animal's comfort and on steady, safe movement through each step. We appreciate the chance to improve, and we are taking your complaint as a useful warning, not as background noise.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
